name: Biejia-Ruangan compound (Chinese herbal tablets)
short: 1,000-person placebo-controlled trial with entecavir: safety profiles did not differ (no figures). Review of 26 studies: no serious adverse reactions. Another: fewer events, CI includes no difference.
text: Biejia-Ruangan is approved in China as an anti-fibrosis traditional Chinese medicine for chronic liver disease and is taken as tablets; the cited abstracts do not list its herbs. In a multicentre, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 1,000 people with chronic hepatitis B and biopsy-confirmed advanced fibrosis or cirrhosis (500 per group) took entecavir with Biejia-Ruangan or with placebo for 72 weeks and could then enter an open-label treatment phase; the follow-up report found no differences in safety profiles between the groups, and the abstracts give no adverse-event numbers. A 2022 meta-analysis of 26 studies (2,717 patients) of Fufang Biejia Ruangan tablets (taken here to be the same compound tablets: the 1,000-person trial's published design report, under the same registration number, calls them tablets of the compound biejia ruangan, abbreviated RGT, and a planned review uses the same abbreviation, RGT, for Fufang Biejia Ruangan Tablet) for hepatitis B liver fibrosis, with placebo named as the comparator, reported no serious adverse reactions. Another 2022 meta-analysis of 8 randomized trials (747 patients) of the compound tablet added to entecavir reported fewer adverse events than with entecavir alone (odds ratio 0.54), but its 95% confidence interval (0.22 to 1.34) includes no difference, although the abstract gives P < .001. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
